gente.contexto: HBS '27, from Monterrey, three years in strategy at a cement group before HBS. Met **last Saturday** at the Harvard Mexas dinner. Offered an intro to a three-person family office in Back Bay that asked her how to bring AI into a family company without the people rejecting it. **You owe her the one-pager.**

Bentley '24, Chief Business Officer at G19 Studio — 14 people in Boston, custom AI for mid-size firms. Runs sales and scoping. Introduced by Prof. Purcell five days ago. First meeting **today 10:00** on Zoom; she asked for "campaigns or content you've made".

Partnerships lead at NEST, a Cambridge hardware incubator (12 companies a cohort). MIT '19. Wrote first after your post; wants "someone who can explain AI to our founders without the hype". First meeting **today 14:15**, 1 Broadway.

Operations director at Grupo Ferra (Monterrey, ~200 people, metal parts). Your sponsor with the board since July. Wrote two days ago with two board questions: data ownership, and what you do when usage drops. **Board decides in two days.**
Plant manager at Grupo Ferra. The real buyer: asked the adoption question twice in the scope meeting. Lost a maintenance system in 2023 to nobody owning it. Put him in the weekly usage review.
Head of Operations at a 300-person logistics firm in Ohio. Cold outreach: opened your first message twice, no reply. Follow-up 2 drafted. Posts about dock-scheduling pain every few weeks.
Founder of a Montreal company that makes inspection cameras for sawmills (40 people). Wrote on LinkedIn that his customers want "AI" and he does not know what to promise. First cold message drafted.
COO of Harrow Distribution, 14 warehouses in New England. Replied yesterday to your cold message: "about a day, and usually wrong". In Boston two days next week — send a time.
Owner of Feldstein Foods (Vermont, 120 people). Bought two AI tools nobody uses. Asked for the short version; you sent it this morning.
Harvard College junior from San Luis Potosí. Offered a seat in the weekly entrepreneurship seminar. **Silent for 9 days** since you asked which week. Waiting for; one nudge, then let it go.
Your CS100 professor. Ex-CTO of a Boston logistics software company. Introduced you to Rebecca Lind; pushes you to finish the Academy application. Office hours once a week at 13:30.
Career coach at CareerEdge, ex-recruiter. Two sessions so far. Her rule: say what changed for the client before what you built. Reads your Academy answers.
MIT '27, co-president of the MIT AI Club. Runs the speaker calendar. Confirmed your spot at Founders & Builders night in two days. The person to ask about a spring talk.

HKS, from Guadalajara. Met last Saturday at the Mexas dinner; works on industrial policy for northern Mexico. Wants to read the Ferra story. Not a client; a bridge to government money for SME training.
MIT Sloan '26, from Monterrey. Met last Saturday. Knows the NEST people; said Matthew Hale is "the one who actually answers mail". Second coffee after the MIT night.
Harvard College senior, Mexico City. Runs the Mexas list and the dinners. Asked you to speak at the spring dinner — answer her this week.
Founder of Ferrous Robotics, NEST cohort. Matthew calls her the skeptic. May stop by today's meeting for ten minutes. Her product: weld inspection arms for small shops.
Bentley '21, associate at a Boston operations consultancy. Met at the alumni panel three weeks ago; he offered to read the one-pager. You never followed up.
VP Operations at a Danish furniture maker's plant in North Carolina (260 people). Posted last week about supervisors drowning in reports. Cold message drafted, not yet in the batch.
EMS101 professor. Moved the case memo two days later. Likes short memos with one recommendation.
CS100 — section with Prof. Purcell's material; Marchetti runs the twice-a-week sessions. Grades on the project, not the exam.
FDS100 professor. Problem set every two weeks; set 6 due in five days.
AI101 professor. Asked you to present the Ferra case to the class in November; date not set.
Your mother, in Monterrey. Wants a photo of the dinner for your grandmother. Calls twice a week at 20:00.
Your brother, 19, studying in Monterrey. Learned to make rice this week, according to your mother.
Your partner at VYNMSA in Monterrey. Runs delivery while you are in Boston; weekly call at the end of the week. Needs the Ferra phase-two scope to staff it.
Associate at a Boston seed fund, met at a Bentley talk two weeks ago. Asked what you would do with the Academy if you got in. No follow-up yet; not a priority until the application is in.
Owner of a 60-person packaging company in Apodaca. Daniela's friend; asked for a call about "what you did at Ferra". After the board decision.
Product lead at a 40-person startup building warehouse robots in **San Francisco**. Met on the Bentley SF trek in August; she offered to show him their pilot playbook.
Founder from Monterrey building supply-chain software in **San Francisco**. Introduced by Ernesto. Wants to compare notes on selling to family companies.
Associate at a seed fund in **San Francisco** that backs industrial AI. Met at a Venture Café session in Cambridge.
Stanford GSB ’26, from Monterrey; same high school. Lives in **San Francisco** and hosts a monthly Latam founders dinner.
Head of ops at a logistics marketplace in **San Francisco**. Commented on his Ferra post; asked how the supervisors were trained.
Engineer at an AI company in **San Francisco** who mentors Bentley students. Reviewed Exo’s agent setup in October.
